label: Mercury
summary: Mercury is a heavy silver liquid metal whose vapour damages the brain, nerves and kidneys. It is in fluorescent tubes and energy-saving bulbs (a few milligrams each), old thermostats and tilt switches (a few grams), and old thermometers, barometers and blood-pressure gauges. Heating it makes it far more dangerous.
signs: A glass tilt switch with a silver liquid bead inside an old round dial thermostat
Fluorescent tubes, compact fluorescent bulbs and UV lamps
Old glass thermometers and barometers with silver liquid
Shiny silver beads on a floor or in a crack
do: Handle tubes and switches gently and keep them whole
If a bulb breaks, open windows and leave the room for at least 15 minutes
Pick up beads and fragments with stiff card and sticky tape
Seal the pickings in a glass jar with a lid and label it
Store mercury items sealed, in a shed or outdoors
For more than one thermometer's worth, or mercury in carpet or floor cracks, close off the room, keep it aired to the outside, and keep children and pregnant women out
dont: Don't vacuum or sweep a spill: it spreads vapour
Don't heat mercury or anything containing it
Don't pour it down a drain or onto the ground
Don't let children play with the beads
Don't wash clothes or shoes that touched mercury, or walk the spill through the house: bag them with the waste
ppe: Dust masks and N95s don’t stop mercury vapour, and it has no smell to warn you; only a mercury (Hg) cartridge does
firstAid: On skin: wash with soap and water
Breathed vapour from a heated or large spill: get to fresh air; coughing, chest pain or shaking afterwards needs medical care
Swallowed a little liquid mercury: don't make them sick; get medical advice; little is absorbed from the gut, but don't wait if they feel unwell
